I'm currently watching Shoujo Kakumei Utena and would like to write out my hypotheses on the first part (episodes 1-13), as well as discuss with anyone willing. There're gonna be spoilers for the first thirteen episodes, but please don't spoil anything past that. For reference, episode thirteen is the recap episode of the Student Council Saga.

CAUTION: Utena spoilers beyond this point!

So, I haven't read any analyses of this show yet because I'm terrible about spoiling myself (I already managed to do so while trying to translate some kanji that appeared in the show...). So, if anyone's around that's well-versed in the analysis of this show, I'd appreciate some insight.

What I'm piecing together so far is that this has all been an allegory for Utena's socialization process. The duel's represent the challenges faced by youths, wherein they must discern what they believe in and are willing to fight for. Utena fought duels for friendship, choice, reason, love, adoration, conviction, and self. What I interpret this to mean is that Utena is fighting to uphold the things that she believes to be good in the world: Friendship, choice over one's own destiny, reason to pursue one's dreams, love, adoration, conviction to be true to oneself, and a strong sense of self. All of her opponents in these duels were the antitheses of these things. Saionji hurt Utena's friend and was abusive to Anthy (but who isn't) and he didn't want her to have reign over her own fate, Miki could not find his reason to play, the orange chick was betrayed and no longer believed in love, Nanami was warped by her adoration of her brother, and Touga tried to destroy Utena's sense of self. Thus, Utena's final victory indicates that her belief in these things has won. Although she lost her first match against Touga, she did regain her self in her rematch.

This show also seems to touch on themes of idealism, which would tie in nicely with Utena's fight for her ideals. It seems that Utena has an idyllic "prince" in her mind that she aspires to be, and this is what gives her power. Perhaps, this is symbolic of the need of role models in the socialization process, or the benefit of having aspirations when one is young. I think that it may have something to do with role models, as Utena is a person who defies societal norms because she is basing herself on a prince. So, she may be an example of counter-socialization. I'm not entirely sure what this all means, but I'm excited for it to come together (at least, I hope I have the mental acuity to do so).

Anyways, just some ramblings on the show so far. I know they don't all make complete sense, but I'm hoping that it'll all make sense to me in the end. Any comments are appreciated!
